sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax for a house in Clarksville?
sections.html:
Owners inside Clarksville pay twice, once to the county and once to the city, and each payment goes to its own office. Values come from the Montgomery County Assessor of Property. The Montgomery County Trustee takes the county share, and the city's Finance and Revenue Department takes the city share.

  • Montgomery County Trustee: Veterans Plaza, 350 Pageant Lane, Suite 101-B, (931) 648-5717. Weekday hours start at 7:30 in the morning and end at 4:30, with extra Saturday mornings in February until noon.
  • Montgomery County Assessor of Property: 350 Pageant Lane, Suite 101-C, phone (931) 648-5709, for name or address corrections and classification questions.
  • City Finance and Revenue: One Public Square, Suite 119, or the North Clarksville Service Center at 111 Cunningham Lane. Call (931) 645-7436 between 8 and 4:30 on weekdays.

The county Trustee collects only the county tax. A house inside Clarksville pays both, and a house outside the city limits pays only the county.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 property tax rates in Clarksville?
sections.html:
The 2026 county rate is $2.10 and the city rate is $1.01, both per $100 of assessed value, for a combined $3.11. The County Commission and City Council adopt rates each July, so an estimate made earlier in the year leans on the previous year's rates.

To estimate a bill, multiply the appraised value by 25 percent, then by 3.11 percent. A house appraised at $263,600, the Census Bureau's median for Clarksville owner-occupied homes, would be assessed at $65,900 and would owe roughly $2,050 in combined county and city tax. Rounding on the real bill can shift the total by a few dollars.

sections.h2: When are Clarksville tax bills due and when do they go delinquent?
sections.html:
The first Monday of October opens the payment season, and February's final day closes the interest-free window. March 1 makes the balance delinquent and starts a charge of 1.5 percent a month, which the county states as 18 percent a year.

The county mails statements in the last week of October, and the city mails its own in October as well. Partial payments on the county bill are allowed starting July 10, as long as the full amount is in by the February deadline, although online county payments must be in full. Owners of record on January 1 are the ones billed, so a house that changed hands later in the year may still show the prior owner's name.

City tax that stays delinquent for a year moves to the delinquent tax attorney, and from then on the Clerk and Master of Montgomery Chancery Court takes the payment at 2 Millennium Plaza, Number 101, (931) 648-5703.

sections.h2: How do you pay a Clarksville property tax bill?
sections.html:
Pay the county bill and the city bill separately, since each office takes only its own.

  • County online: e-check carries 1.75 percent plus $1.00, and Visa or Mastercard carries 2.65 percent plus $1.00.
  • County by mail or drop box: checks, cashier's checks and money orders only in the 24 hour drop box outside the Trustee's office.
  • County at banks: F and M Bank, Planters Bank, Cumberland Bank and Trust, and United Community Bank take full payments through February 28, 2027, with the original bill.
  • City: online with a 2.5 percent processor fee, by mail to P.O. Box 30549 in Clarksville, or at the Revenue Office or the drop box left of City Hall's main doors.

The city refunds an overpayment to whoever paid second. If a mortgage servicer pays in December and the owner also pays in February, the refund goes to the servicer first.

sections.h2: What tax relief can Clarksville homeowners use?
sections.html:
Two state programs can help a Clarksville homeowner: Tax Relief and Tax Freeze. Relief pays back part of the tax for elderly and disabled owners, disabled veterans and their surviving spouses, while Freeze fixes the bill at the amount for the year the owner first qualified.

Applications for Tax Relief are available at both the Trustee's office and the city Finance and Revenue office, and a first-time applicant only needs to sign up at one of them. Tax Freeze sign-up happens at the County Trustee's office, which tells the city if you qualify. Recipients must send in a voucher each year to both the county and the city, because the state uses those vouchers to repay the covered share. Call (931) 645-7436 for the city side.

sections.h2: What happens when Clarksville taxes stay unpaid?
sections.html:
An unpaid bill can end in a public auction of the house. Parcels with taxes two or more years behind are eligible for the Montgomery County tax sale, held at the Montgomery County Courts Center at 2 Millennium Plaza.

The Chancery Court orders the sale for cash, and the former owner, a lien holder or heirs have one year to redeem by paying taxes, interest, penalties and costs. The redemption price carries up to 10 percent interest a year. Except for state and federal liens, other liens are cleared by the sale. The city adds that the house can be sold at auction no matter who was supposed to pay under a contract, so a buyer's promise to pay does not protect the property.

sections.h2: What is Clarksville like for a homeowner?
sections.html:
Clarksville serves as seat of Montgomery County and is its sole incorporated municipality. It lies on the Cumberland River, anchors a metropolitan area that spills into Kentucky, and borders Fort Campbell. Its nickname is Queen of the Cumberland, and Austin Peay State University is in town. The Leaf-Chronicle, described as Tennessee's oldest newspaper, is published here.

Growth has been quick. The Census Bureau counted 132,929 people in 2010, 166,722 in 2020 and estimated 188,829 in July 2025, spread over about 99 square miles of land. Interstate 24 and U.S. Highway 79 carry much of the commercial growth, and the mean commute is 27 minutes.

Survey data for 2020 to 2024 list 67,832 households, 22,758 veterans and a $69,303 median household income. Renters pay a median $1,307, and owners live in 55.6 percent of homes.

sections.h2: How do taxes work when you sell a Clarksville house?
sections.html:
The county Trustee points new owners to the closing statement to learn who pays for the year of transfer, and any unpaid tax stays on the property. A closing agent can request payoffs from the Trustee and the city and settle them out of the proceeds.

Ask for a calculation of the portion of the calendar year each party owns the house. The county Assessor posts a proration calculator that divides the year at a chosen date, which gives a starting number to compare with the closing statement.

faqs.q: What is the Clarksville property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: Montgomery County charges $2.10 and the city charges $1.01 for 2026, both per $100 of assessed value. A house inside Clarksville therefore pays $3.11 per $100, applied to 25 percent of its appraised value.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Clarksville city property tax?
faqs.a: Bring it to Finance and Revenue at One Public Square, Suite 119, or to the North Clarksville Service Center on Cunningham Lane. Mail to P.O. Box 30549 also works, as does the online portal with its 2.5 percent fee.

faqs.q: Do I pay the Montgomery County Trustee and the city separately?
faqs.a: Yes. The Trustee collects only county tax, and the city collects its own tax. A house inside Clarksville receives two bills and each must be paid to its own office.

faqs.q: How long before Clarksville can sell a house for unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Properties with taxes delinquent two or more years are eligible for the Montgomery County tax sale. After a sale the owner has a one year redemption period.

faqs.q: Who can I call about my Clarksville assessment?
faqs.a: The Montgomery County Assessor of Property answers at (931) 648-5709. Formal appeals go to the county Board of Equalization, which generally opens June 1, and the Assessor knows the filing cutoff.
